newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 24.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 24. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

A regent from the Yogyakarta province has admitted he was approached by a number of people to donate one billion rupiah to a charitable foundation run by President Suharto if he wanted to be reappointed for a second term.

National Police Chief Lieutenant-General Dibyo Widodo said the number of crimes reported dropped this year and he predicted armed robberies, drugs and student brawls would continue to dominate the country's crime pattern next year.
Bank Indonesia has announced new regulations that would provide better protection for depositors if a bank is shut down.

The Indonesian Textile Association has asked that the government's target for textile exports by the end of the current sixth five-year 1998/99 plan be revised down to $8 billion from $10 billion after earlier being cut from $12 billion as the figure could not be reached.

The flow of truck traffic through the West Java port of Merak across the Sunda Strait to Lampung on the tip of Sumatra has returned to normal after a charter ship was engaged after bad weather slow smaller vessles and caused thousands of vehicles to bank up last week in an unprecedented jam.

Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said his department had not yet received any report from two Canadian mining companies, Bre-X and Barrick, regarding the results of their negotiations over the huge Busang gold find in Kalimantan.
